apps.name: Vine
apps.current_status: shut down January 17, 2017; archived content accessible through Internet Archive
decline_reasons: poor monetization strategy
management issues under Twitter ownership
competition from emerging platforms like TikTok and Instagram Reels
failure to adapt to market demands
apps.community_size: Legacy creator community migrated to YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram; estimated 1.5 billion daily video loops at peak

apps.name: Winamp
apps.current_status: still maintained and actively developed; undergoing modernization for streaming era
decline_reasons: transition from downloads to music streaming services
competition from cloud-based media players
market shift to mobile and streaming platforms
apps.community_size: 80-83 million active users globally; CEO target is 250 million users; open source initiative in 2024

apps.name: iTunes
apps.current_status: phased out starting 2019 with macOS Catalina; split into Music, Podcasts, and Apple TV; legacy versions still available
decline_reasons: dominance of music streaming services like Spotify and Apple Music
poor user interface and increasingly bloated software
shift away from digital downloads to subscription models
apps.community_size: 29.8 million legacy followers; significant legacy user base with ongoing concerns about media library access

apps.name: Skype
apps.peak_users: 300 million peak; 40 million daily active users at peak
apps.current_status: being retired May 5, 2025; users directed to Microsoft Teams
decline_reasons: competition from Microsoft Teams, Discord, and Zoom
Microsoft's strategic pivot to Teams as primary communication platform
fragmented messaging market with better alternatives
website traffic dropped 10% between 2021-2022
apps.community_size: 36 million daily active users as of 2023; 300 million monthly active users reported for 2024; 8.6 million in software sector

apps.name: Evernote
apps.current_status: declining downloads but maintains substantial active user base; version 10 update caused significant user churn
decline_reasons: pricing structure changes and subscription model adjustments
problematic v10 software update that lost features
competition from modern alternatives like Notion, OneNote, and Obsidian
deteriorating user experience and feature limitations
apps.community_size: 225 million active users globally; loyal legacy user base remains committed despite frustrations; community forum active with discussions

apps.name: Pidgin
apps.current_status: declining but actively maintained; used in privacy-focused OS Tails; multi-protocol messaging client
decline_reasons: API shutdowns from major chat services like Facebook and AIM
consolidation of messaging services into centralized platforms
shift to modern messaging apps with mobile-first design
loss of platform connectivity as networks shut down legacy APIs
apps.community_size: Active developer and user community; integrated into security-focused operating systems; forum and documentation maintained

apps.name: Miranda IM
apps.peak_users: Millions of users across Windows (exact numbers unavailable)
apps.current_status: original project no longer maintained; successfully forked to Miranda NG with active community development
decline_reasons: slow development pace of original project
shift to centralized messaging platforms
decline of traditional instant messaging protocols
resource-intensive development model
apps.community_size: Miranda NG maintains active community; 350+ plugins available; community forums, wiki, and social media presence active; dedicated developer team

apps.name: Adobe Flash
apps.current_status: officially discontinued December 2020; emulated through open-source Ruffle project; enterprise versions available in select regions
decline_reasons: critical security vulnerabilities and exploits
shift to web standards (HTML5, CSS, JavaScript)
poor performance and resource consumption
mobile platform incompatibility
browser abandonment of Flash support
apps.community_size: Open-source Ruffle emulator project continues active development in 2024; enterprise support in China (Zhongcheng) and for international enterprise users (Harman International)
